claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloy is in an ordered, single-phase hexagonal state.
The as-deposited alloy exhibits a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited transition produces a large but abrupt magnetocaloric entropy change.
Controlled low-temperature annealing can enhance short-range chemical ordering in the as-deposited alloy.
Controlled low-temperature annealing can induce subtle nanoscale phase separation in the as-deposited alloy.
Controlled low-temperature annealing can alter the grain size or cause modest grain coarsening.
The proposed annealing-induced microstructural changes can occur without changing the bulk single-phase hexagonal state.
Annealing-induced microstructural refinement alters the alloy's local energy landscape.
The altered local energy landscape broadens the magnetostructural transition.
Broadening or distributing the transformation makes the magnetocaloric response less abrupt.
Broadening or distributing the transformation reduces hysteretic losses.
Annealing will make the magnetocaloric transition more reversible than in the as-deposited baseline.
The annealed alloy will preserve a substantial magnetocaloric response.
Annealing may modestly decrease the peak entropy change.
The predictions apply only while the original single-phase hexagonal state and mechanical stability are retained.
The predictions are restricted to low-applied-field cooling cycles near the magnetostructural transition temperature.
The magnitude of transition broadening and hysteresis reduction depends sensitively on the annealing parameters.
